fields.why: Besides eJRF and outbreak case counts (count/rate), the report computes its own proportion of high-incidence countries that introduced TCV (three [7%] of 44), a program measure that is binary/categorical.

In a limited report only the article's own results count; the group comparisons (WHO regions, age groups, study sites) are cited GBD and population-study estimates. The only own contrast is eJRF cases 2018 vs 2021, a reporting increase, not the basis for B's group comparison.

B's group framework rests on cited regional or age-group incidence (GBD, Table 1); the article compares nothing of its own across three or more groups. At most a pair (eJRF 2018 vs 2021) could be argued.
All CIs (GBD 9.2 million, Table 1 incidences) are cited from other studies; the report computes no CI or test itself.

Agreed surveillance/descriptive; review or synthesis fits the narrative synthesis of population-based and modeling estimates, while evaluation or monitoring is defensible for a 'Progress Toward' report measured against WHO's prioritization of 44 high-incidence countries, though no numeric target is stated.
Income appears only as country income level (World Bank, Gavi eligibility) and country-level WASH access, which the brief classes as geography, not SES.
WASH access, competing priorities and Gavi financial barriers explain country-level burden or delayed vaccine introduction, not a disparity or an SPD group's outcome.
The only age-group ranking (5–9, 10–14, 1–4 years) is GBD incidence cited from another source (footnote ††); a limited report's cited figures are not its own results.
Follows from no groupwise entry: the age ranking is cited GBD data.
